questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew I wanted to go to Asia. Preferably to Japan, but as that did not work out, South Korea was my second choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Honestly, there was not that much information, however, it is straight forward: Get the required documents by the university by email, apply for a visa, figure out your living situation (Airbnb, dorm, etc), apply for courses at the university(the application period opens close to semester start and its can be very competitive with only a few slots per course), enjoy your stay!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an orientation session. Go there and try to get a slot for the afterparty as well!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I just looked on Airbnb. Better look earlier than later.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very convenient, because the public transport is so great! Just make sure you consider if you want to live in Seoul or Suwon, depending on the courses you take (science courses are at the Suwon campus). I would 1000% recommend living in Seoul if you can, because Suwon is pretty dead, from what I have heard.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You do everything through the mobility portal

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I guess you can always send emails and ask for any help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The application can be somewhat competitive, as they sometimes offer only a few slots for exchange students. And make sure the course you want to take is in English if you can't speak Korean!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was not happy with the professors in all of my courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The workload was similar to KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had offline classes and needed to watch video lectures before each one of them. Its basically half-online, half-offline. Depending on the course, you also need to do regular hand-ins, midterms and finals.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
AI in Marketing (Not recommended, even though I got a good grade)
AI in Human Rights
Introductory Statistics for Data Science

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the Statistics course. Its a lot of R programming, but the professor was motivated and always helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a few events hosted by an international committee. They are very nice, but Seoul itself hosts many cool events (drone shows, light shows, etc)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were trips with activities, but very limited slots, sports day, university festival, some parties, and a few more

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Eat ramen at the Han River, watch a drone show, and if you are into League of Legends, definitely go to LoL Park and watch LCK. And enjoy good food, soyu (would recommend the cheongju with white wine though)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The things mentioned above

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy if you are familiar with asian culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Honestly, everything. I would have loved to stay there :)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do your research early!
Remember that there is sooo much to do and you can't do everything during the semester. Just enjoy the moments you have!
Don't stress too much. It's gonna be amazing!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't think there is more than I already said.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: There is not one specific thing. I am just very grateful to have had the opportunity.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Going back home :(

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
